cards.text: Then the LORD speaks to Moses, Israel's leader. He has a blessing for His people, and Moses isn't the one who's supposed to give it. So who gets the job?

cards.question: The LORD wants Moses to pass these words along. Who is Moses supposed to tell?

cards.text: Aaron and his sons, the priests, get the exact words from God: "This is how you are to bless the Israelites." Honestly, THANK YOU, because when I make one up myself it comes out "May your edges be crisp and your middle stay soft."

cards.question: God has handed Aaron and his sons the words of the blessing. How are they supposed to get those words to the Israelites?

cards.text: So here's line one: "May the LORD bless you and keep you;" Short and simple, and I'd stamp it on every cookie if it would fit.
Line two asks the LORD to shine on His people and be gracious to them. Friend, I spent YEARS in the back of a dark junk drawer, so trust me, light shining on you hits different.

And line three: "may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and give you peace." Peace! The dead batteries I shared that drawer with argued ALL NIGHT over who had the most charge left, so I would have LOVED some of that.

cards.question: In the priests' blessing, lines two and three both picture the LORD's ___ turned toward His people.
True or false: every line of the priests' blessing is about what the LORD does for His people.

cards.text: Now God tells Moses what happens when the priests say these words. Lean in, friend, this is the good part.

cards.question: When Aaron and his sons speak this blessing, what does God say they're putting on the Israelites?
True or false: in the end, Aaron and his sons are the ones who make the blessing on the Israelites happen.
